Old paint in Oak Lawn, and how it has to be handled

Old paint is the thing to know about here. Oak Lawn is largely 1960s housing, and anything painted before 1978 may have lead in the layers underneath. It is handled rather than avoided: the room is closed off, the dust is contained while the work happens, and the site is cleaned to a set standard before anyone leaves.

The practical content of it is dust. Where paint in an Oak Lawn room gets disturbed past about six square feet, twenty outside, or wherever a window comes out, the work has to be contained and cleaned to a standard. That is time at both ends of the job, and it is why an honest quote on 17,940 homes worth of 1967-median housing reads longer than a fast one.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Oak Lawn.

Of the 23,115 housing units counted in Oak Lawn, 78.3 percent went up before 1980. There is no pre-1978 bucket, so 1980 is the nearest line the Census draws for Oak Lawn. The federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule applies to work that disturbs paint in housing built before 1978, and in Illinois the EPA administers it directly rather than through a state program.

None of that is a reason to leave an Oak Lawn house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Questions

Asked about Oak Lawn

What changes the price most on a house here?

Condition, not size. On 1967-median stock in Oak Lawn what varies is how much has to come off or be made good before anything goes on: loose paint, failed caulk, damaged trim, ceilings that have been patched before. Two houses on the same street can differ by a lot on that alone.

Does the lead-safe rule apply to my house in Oak Lawn?

Probably, and the honest answer is that your build year decides it rather than the town. 78.3 percent of housing units in Oak Lawn went up before 1980, so most addresses here land on the pre-1978 side of the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule. It applies to work that disturbs paint, at roughly six square feet per room inside or twenty square feet outside, and to any window replacement. Check the year on your own address and ask whoever quotes you how they handle it.

Most of Oak Lawn is owner occupied. Does that change anything?

It changes what the work usually is. At 82.5 percent owner occupied, with 17,940 owner households, there is very little turnover painting here and a lot of repeat maintenance: exteriors on a cycle, one room at a time inside, trim and doors when they finally go. A maintained house and a neglected one are different jobs and should be different numbers, in both directions.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Oak Lawn is 3.3 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.
